steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9 inch pie or cake pan.
In a large bowl, mix together flour, milk, eggs butter and salt. Stir until smooth. Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake in preheated oven for 10 minutes. Reduce heat to 325 degrees cooking for additional 5 minutes. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Seattle Dutch Babies
raw_recipe.description: A rich popover pancake served with melted butter, powder sugar, lemon wedges or fresh fruit. A dish that's well known in Seattle, Washington.

video.description: Only 5 ingredients need be mixed together to create this incredibly delicious and easy dutch baby pancake! Simply combine flour, milk, salt, eggs and butter into a smooth batter, pour into a pan and bake. Serve hot with maple syrup, powdered sugar or your favorite preserves. So easy to prepare, this delicious breakfast or brunch item is ready in minutes!

review.reviewBody:
I make this for overnight guests and it never fails. However, I usually bake it at 425 F for 25 minutes. 

We always serve it with powdered sugar and lemon or lime wedges squeezed over the top of the finished Baby. Also, I add 1/4 tsp. vanilla to the batter and preheat the pan. I melt the butter in the pan in the oven and pour the batter into the hot pan (after rolling the pan to spread the butter evenly).

Cast iron pan was key. I heated the oven to 450. I put the cast iron pan in the oven with the butter to melt the butter. Then I added the batter and lowered the temp to 400 and it came out perfect after 20 minutes. I could have lowered to 425 but I wasn't sure. Another reader said 425.

This gets 5 stars because it was delicious! Creamy custard like texture that paired well with sautéed apples seasoned with sugar and cinnamon! I thickened a little apple juice with cornstarch and combined with the apples before pouring over the Dutch baby after it came out of the oven to make a nice sauce. I found the baking temperature to be way off! I had to crank the oven up to 400 and even after it started to look puffed I had to finish it with my convection oven setting still at 400 F. Even so, it is so good we will be having this again often!

Let me start by saying I had never had a Dutch Baby until I made this recipe. I made it for the first time last week and followed the directions exactly, except that I had to nearly double the cooking time. I came back to AR and looked at other reviews and decided to try again. So, I made this recipe again last night and added 1/4 tsp of cinnamon and 1/4 tsp of vanilla. I also melted one Tbsp butter in a glass pie plate in the oven while the oven was heating up. I then poured in the batter, added about 15 minutes to the cooking time, and wow! They really puffed up this time and had a much better consistency and taste. I just served with butter and a little powdered sugar. I will definitely be making these again and again!

This is so good and so easy! I took the advice of another reviewer and cooked it at 425 for 25 min. as well as melting the butter in my pan before adding the mix to it and it came out perfect. I did add a splash of vanilla for some extra taste. If I were to do anything different it would be maybe try making it in a 10 in. pan instead as it puffed up so much on the sides it collapsed in one spot.

This turned out great! I put a little bit of butter in my glass pie plate in the oven, then poured the batter in. I added 1/4 tsp. Cinnamon and 3/4 tsp. Vanilla extract into the batter. I also added a few tbsp. Sugar and baked it for 25 minutes. We put powdered sugar and chopped strawberries and bananas on it. My family ate the whole thing!!!

I cut the butter down to 1 T and used soymilk... sprinkled sugar and cinnimon on top before baking. I warmed the eggs in a bowl of water and heated the milk in the microwave. I also heated my pan in the oven for a few minutes. I baked at 425 for 15 minutes and then turned it down to 375 for the last 7. I like this recipe better than the recipe that came my "Oven Pancake Pan" which calls for 6 eggs, 1 c flour, 1 c milk, 2 T sugar and longer baking time. This recipe is lighter and less eggy. Thanks, Anneliese.

I've made dutch babies using this recipe 3 or 4 times now. The first time they puffed up well. The 2nd time, not so much. I think the pan you use makes a big difference. When I used a glass pan they tended not to puff up as much. I don't have a cast iron pan, so I used an Emile Henry baking dish this last time and they puffed up fantastically. I also followed recommendations to heat the oven higher (I went to 425). I lowered the temp back to 325 after about 15 minutes and cooked for 10 more minutes. The visual results are stunning with the big puffy crust. We usually eat these with a combination of powdered sugar plus lemon juice or brown sugar plus a little butter. Or, we top with berries and whip cream.

This always makes me feel like a champ in the kitchen. Her recipe is fail-safe. I put it all in the food processor and whirl together for less than one minute, then do the rest exactly the same. Be sure to do the additional 5 minutes at 325 - I skipped that twice and the third time did so, and it was MUCH better - the sides got crispy. BRAVO WOMAN - 

UPDATE: Did a pair of Dutch Babies in the small #4 cast irons, they came out magnificent with both of them riding the sides of pans. We had two baby Dutch Babies! YUMMMILLY

Loved this! Fast and easy. My VERY picky grandson who never eats more than a few bites of anything, asked for and ate seconds! I served it with a Blueberry sauce made by adding 1 cup of Maple Syrup and 1 1/2 Cups of Frozen Blueberries and bringing it to a boil over med/low heat, and boiled it for a minute or two. It was a Hit!
I make this recipe quite often and because I’m at high altitude (7,500 ft) I always add 1/2 tsp. baking powder and it “puffs.” Definitely need this otherwise it turns out flat.
I suggest a little lemon juice, and a bit of vanilla for flavor. cinnamon sugar is a great topper too.
Quick and easy Would like it to puff up a little going to try baking soda and powder next time Wonderful w strawberries

I should have read the reviews. I thought that the temps were too low. I think the person who submitted this recipe got them flipped. You should start at 425 and drop to 375. Mine stuck to the pan and that usually doesn’t happen when I cook it at higher temperatures.
I made it it cooked quicker than my other recipe but it just didn’t seem like it was done and it never got really poufy at all

I agree this needs to be cooked at a higher temp-425 works for me. I put all the butter, plus a bit, into the preheating oven. It melts quickly, so remove it and then you can pour it right into your batter and brush the bit left in the pan to grease it.
it is delicious but was not cooking and puffing up.....the temp should be at least 425, not 375 and it takes at least 25 minutes not 10.
I like lemon juice, butter, powdered sugar and bananas
So easy! I baked at 425 for the first 10 minutes and then dropped the temp to 375 for the last 5 minutes. They were delicious.
This is good but as others have said I turned the heat to 425. And cooked for 20-25 minutes
